patterns.name: Explore → Narrow → Build → Ship or Stall
patterns.description: Work starts as broad exploration or asset cataloging, narrows into a concrete MVP/positioning, moves into active prototyping and demo/pitch prep, then either advances into sales/productization or settles into long-term maintenance/archival.
triggers: Possession of an asset or identifiable opportunity (dataset, prototype, program concept)
A concrete monetization or launch milestone (demo deadline, accelerator app, cohort date)

phases.description: Exploration / inventory (collect data, list options, high-level ideas)
Scope narrowing (choose target use case / positioning / monetization path)
Prototype / demo build (MVP + demo scripts, technical PoC)
Go-to-market / pitch (outreach, accelerator applications, pricing targets)
Outcome: ship (paid pilots / productization) or stall/archive

patterns.name: Tool evaluation → integrate → standardize
patterns.description: The user surveys several tooling/library options, experiments with a subset for concrete use cases, then consolidates a preferred stack and integrates those tools across projects. The process is multi-stage and spans weeks to months, with tools then appearing as recurring dependencies.
triggers: A concrete project need (RAG, embeddings, graph storage)
Comparative questions about tradeoffs or capabilities

phases.description: Initial discovery / list of candidate tools
Focused evaluation / small proofs-of-concept
Recommendation and decision (pick one or complementary set)
Integration across projects and reuse

patterns.name: Intense Short Sprint → Dormancy / Handoff
patterns.description: A concentrated, high-frequency burst of work and rapid transitions (multiple commits/updates in days), followed by a sharp drop in activity where the project either gets handed off, archived, or enters long quiet periods.
triggers: Need to produce a demo, benchmark, or literaturereview in short order
Time-boxed opportunity (demo deadline, conference, cohort start)

phases.description: High-intensity sprint (many rapid updates/changes)
Immediate deliverable / demo or handoff
Prolonged low-activity / monitoring or archival

patterns.name: Asset → Monetization Push
patterns.description: When a nontrivial data asset, productized capability, or curriculum exists the person quickly pivots toward explicit monetization experiments: pricing hypotheses, outreach drafts, paid pilots and sales targets are created and prioritized.
triggers: Realization of a collectible/unique asset (large dataset, established cohort, working backend)
Near-term revenue target or short runway / quick-win imperative

phases.description: Recognition of an asset (dataset, curriculum, unique capability)
Ideation of monetization paths (SaaS, agency, one-off packs)
Go-to-market materials and outreach (email drafts, pricing, KPIs)
Early sales/pilot experiments and measurement

patterns.name: Cascading Project Spawn from a Core Idea
patterns.description: A single core project idea spawns multiple related entities (org, pitch deck, application, tooling procurement, IP decisions) in a short time window — work fractures into many parallel threads to cover product, legal, fundraising, and operational needs.
triggers: Decision to pursue funding or formalize a product
Application to accelerators or public-facing commitments
Recognition that multiple operational/legal threads must be handled concurrently

phases.description: Core project conception or consolidation
Immediate parallelization into complementary tracks (branding/org, pitch materials, pilot planning, tooling, IP)
Synchronized short sprints across tracks
Cross-track updates and re-alignment (e.g., pivoting GTM impacts pitch and pilots)

patterns.name: Pick-One-And-Go-All-In → Later Question Suitability
patterns.description: The person frequently gravitates to a single 'best' tool or pattern for immediate velocity (goes all-in for demos/prototyping) and only after usage begins to surface production tradeoffs (cost, concurrency, maintainability) that prompt re-evaluation.
triggers: Need for rapid prototyping or instructor/curriculum demo
Time pressure to produce visible output (demo, cohort, pitch)

phases.description: Select a single tool/stack to maximize speed
Deep implementation and integration for demo/MVP
Encounter scaling/cost/ops limits
Re-assess and either augment with alternatives or accept tradeoffs

patterns.name: Exploration → Shortlist → Commit
patterns.description: The user moves from broad exploration of options into an evaluated shortlist and then converts that shortlist into an explicit, dated project with concrete logistics and next steps. The move from fuzzy idea to concrete project is deliberate and often fast once a preferred option emerges.
triggers: Decision pressure (time-bound need like travel dates or internship start)
A new opportunity appearing (internship, program schedule)
Desire to test a hypothesis quickly (contrast experiment)

phases.description: Broad exploration / options brainstorm (many alternatives considered)
Shortlist & prioritized tradeoffs (preferred ordering emerges)
Operationalization into an explicit project (start/end dates, checklists, tasks)
Early execution or re-evaluation after arrival

patterns.name: Single-day intense debugging burst
patterns.description: Short, highly-focused debugging or engineering sessions where a problem is investigated and a concrete workaround or change is proposed/implemented the same day. These bursts produce multiple rapid state changes (creation + several updates) and often close quickly.
triggers: Immediate technical failure or blocker (error logs, LookupError, inconsistent hardware output)
Availability of a quick, testable hypothesis or workaround

phases.description: Problem observed or error reported
Rapid diagnosis and exploratory edits/experiments
One or more immediate fixes/workarounds implemented
Short follow-up / monitoring

patterns.name: Prototype spike → handoff / long tail
patterns.description: An upfront concentrated prototyping and shipping phase (high activity density at the start) that culminates in a release or proof-of-concept, followed by a low-activity maintenance/iteration tail. Early work is intense and outcome-oriented; later work is incremental.
triggers: Clear technical feasibility and a reusable infra (existing pipelines like SponsorFind)
Short-term deliverable or release target (publish to GitHub, demo notebook)

phases.description: Rapid prototyping and intense iteration (design + demo)
Release / publish a v0 or demo
Bugfixes, small enhancements, documentation updates
Long-tail maintenance or deprioritization

patterns.name: Productization sprint and iterative scaling
patterns.description: After early validation, the user pivots from exploratory or coaching activity to a productized offering. This pattern features a time-boxed launch sprint, coordinated marketing and operations tasks, and ongoing iteration focused on revenue/scale metrics.
triggers: Sufficient early traction or revenue signal
Aiming to convert an existing activity into repeatable revenue (summer program deadlines)

phases.description: Validate demand and define positioning (audience, outcomes)
Design a productized format and schedule (program/curriculum)
Time-boxed launch sprint (marketing, assets, enrollment)
Iterate on conversion, delivery, and scaling metrics

patterns.name: Research → Pragmatic Prototype
patterns.description: Starts as a technical/architectural research conversation, quickly narrows to a pragmatic stack, and moves to prototyping/testing with hosted or OSS tools rather than building complex bespoke systems.
triggers: A concrete engineering problem or demo objective appears
Desire to validate functionality quickly or avoid long implementation
Resource/time constraints that favor hosted/OSS choices

phases.description: Discovery / architecture sketch: high-level problem framing and possible components
Tradeoff comparison: list blockers and concrete candidate technologies
Pragmatic selection: choose an accessible hosted/OSS option to reduce build time
Prototype / test: create a small end-to-end test or experiment
Decide: adopt the pragmatic option for MVP or continue evaluation

patterns.name: Multi-option Tool Triage → Pick One and Go All-in
patterns.description: When faced with a tooling need the user quickly generates a short shortlist (typically 3+), runs focused comparisons/tests, then designates a recommended tool and moves into integration or deeper testing.
triggers: A new technical requirement (e.g., OCR, browser automation)
Need to prototype or build an MVP quickly
Unknown constraints (performance/scale/authentication) that demand empirical comparison

phases.description: Problem definition and success criteria for tooling
Shortlist 3+ candidate tools or services
Short focused evaluations / tests
Declare recommended choice (and sometimes keep alternates)
Integrate or continue with the chosen tool

patterns.name: Concept Deepening → Cross-Project Reuse
patterns.description: An initially discussed concept is rapidly deepened through technical write-ups and examples, after which it becomes a canonical solution referenced across multiple projects and integrations.
triggers: A recurring technical need across projects
Request for more depth (e.g., to apply the concept in code or architecture)
Opportunity to reuse a pattern across multiple active efforts

phases.description: Initial introduction of the concept
Technical deepening: detailed explanations, applied workflows, and edge-cases
Concrete applied workflows or patterns are authored
Cross-project references and reuse across multiple initiatives

patterns.name: Academy → Spin-out / Productize
patterns.description: Ideas originating in the educational/academy context are rapidly shaped into commercial offers, pilots, or grant mechanisms — often with concrete pricing, pilot structures, and marketing assets.
triggers: Desire to monetize or operationalize academy output
Need for a talent pipeline or real-world project work
Opportunity to convert teaching content into customer-facing services

phases.description: Idea surfaced within academy/curriculum context
Scope and incentive design (grants, externships, comp plans)
MVP/offer definition (pricing, trial sprint, target customers)
Go-to-market preparation (brochures, outreach copy)
Pilot/launch / talent onboarding

patterns.name: Fast Pivot to MVP & Traction
patterns.description: When early signals or a product idea emerge the user favors rapid pivots to the fastest possible validation path (small product change, focused MVP) and records early traction metrics quickly.
triggers: Need for quick validation or revenue
Discovery of a clearer, faster-to-build value proposition
Time/resource pressure to show progress

phases.description: Idea or problem reframing with attention to fastest-validation path
Small scope pivot to an MVP that can be shipped quickly
Capture early traction / metrics
Decide next step based on traction (iterate, scale, or re-evaluate)

patterns.name: Exploration burst → Scope narrowing → Build/Integrate
patterns.description: Rapid ideation and architecture work followed by explicit scoping and selection of tech/requirements, then transition into concrete implementation or integration work (often with lower cadence). This is the classic 'idea → PRD → prototype' arc.
triggers: new product idea or application (e.g., applying to an accelerator, new project to solve)
recognition of an opportunity or gap that rewards a concrete design
need to produce artifacts (PRD, MVP, resume bullets) quickly

phases.description: Exploration / brainstorming (high frequency ideas, many options considered)
Scope-narrowing / PRD (choose architecture, prioritize MVP features and tech candidates)
Build / integrate (implement prototypes, wire up chosen tools; cadence drops relative to burst)

patterns.name: Multi-option tool evaluation → pick one → integrate (with occasional replacement)
patterns.description: User considers several candidate tools/services, runs short evaluations, then selects one to embed into the product/stack; later the chosen tool may be replaced or re-evaluated as needs change.
triggers: a clear capability need (lead enrichment, enrichment/contact intelligence, LLM backbone, email hosting)
project stage where dependencies must be chosen for the MVP or process

phases.description: Survey of 2+ candidate tools
Short trials/assessments (compatibility, cost, fit)
Selection and integration into design
Occasional re-evaluation or replacement as requirements evolve

patterns.name: Blocked-by-environment friction (install / dependency stalls)
patterns.description: Attempts to run or adopt a tool are halted by local environment, dependency, or configuration problems. The user or assistant documents fixes or workarounds, but progress pauses until infra issues are resolved.
triggers: moving from conceptual discussion to hands-on local dev work or integration
introducing third-party packages or platform-specific tooling

phases.description: Attempt to use/install tool
Encounter environment/dependency friction (missing PATH, Python, DNS/Manage UI, incompatible package imports)
Problem diagnosis and provision of remediation steps
Delay while environment is fixed (may resolve or remain blocked)

patterns.name: Short deadline-driven ideation sprints
patterns.description: Very short, intense sessions focused on a specific deliverable (application answers, demo scripts, concise narratives). These are rapid, tightly-scoped efforts meant to produce polished outputs quickly.
triggers: application deadlines or submission opportunities
need for a short, persuasive artifact (demo script, application answers)

phases.description: Rapid brainstorming (hours–days)
Refinement and drafting (concise editing to match format/style)
Delivery or storage of artifacts (answers, scripts, curated examples)
Follow-up or reuse later (occasional long-delayed revisit)

patterns.name: Long-running theme with heavy early activity and sporadic maintenance
patterns.description: Projects that become long-term themes: intense early planning and architecture activity followed by a much lower but persistent cadence of updates over months (resume updates, occasional integration notes).
triggers: internships, ongoing product initiatives, or strategic bets that require multi-month attention
projects that produce durable value (resume items, core infra)

phases.description: Launch / heavy planning and design (burst of activity upfront)
Sustained low-cadence maintenance and incremental updates
Occasional major updates (resume bullets, funding notes, late integrations)

patterns.name: Rapid Prototyping Burst
patterns.description: Short, intense bursts of activity where an entity is created and receives many updates in a very small window (hours–days), producing a working draft/prototype or a concrete configuration quickly, then quiets down.
triggers: Immediate operational need (e.g., provisioning email/domain)
Small scoped creative task or proof-of-concept request
Time-limited opportunity (travel planning, demo, quick content update)

phases.description: Spark/creation: idea or need appears and entity is created
High-density iteration: many focused updates/edits in a short window (hours–days) to get a working artifact
Stabilization/quiet: activity drops sharply; the item sits in a usable but not heavily-evolved state

patterns.name: Idea Incubation → MVP/Productization
patterns.description: An early-stage idea progresses over many small updates from vague concept to scoped MVP, then to product packaging and GTM assets; updates are spread out across weeks with repeated reframing.
triggers: Desire to productize expertise/services
Perceived high-leverage business opportunity or revenue target
Requests for a single long-term focus or flagship project

phases.description: Concepting: high-level framing and opportunity identification
Scoping: define offerings, scope MVP, pricing and delivery model
Build planning & prototyping: architecture and minimal hackathon-style MVPs
GTM & productization: creation of assets, pricing, outreach and positioning

patterns.name: Pragmatic Simplification / Lean Pivot
patterns.description: After detailed architectural or technical planning, the user deliberately pivots toward a leaner, no-code or minimal-ops path to get early value quickly instead of executing a complex full-build.
triggers: Recognition of engineering cost, resource limits, or slow performance
Desire for a quick demo/MVP or to de-risk a hypothesis
Blocked-by-gating (e.g., gated Llama repos) or technical impracticality

phases.description: Ambitious design: propose a full-featured, complex architecture
Reality check: identify cost/time/complexity constraints
Lean pivot: select no-code/managed services or lighter technical approaches for faster iteration and validation
Iterate: use insights from the lean approach to refine future technical choices

patterns.name: Long-running Iterative Development with Periodic Re-evaluation
patterns.description: Projects that persist over months with recurring updates: slow, deliberate progress involving architecture changes, repeated reframing, and intermittent bursts of activity (weeks → months).
triggers: Designation as a top-priority or flagship project
Research/engineering complexity requiring staged progress
Ongoing external goals (journal target, revenue target, MVP roadmap)

phases.description: Launch/commit: project is identified as a multi-month priority
Iteration cycles: periodic updates, sprint-like refinements, & new decisions
Re-evaluation: architecture or scope is revisited and adjusted
Continuation or reprioritization: project remains active or is moved to a new phase

patterns.name: Very short focused execution sprints (single-day hardening)
patterns.description: The user launches short, intense technical sprints that quickly produce hardened artifacts (scripts, evaluation pipelines, figures), often iterating multiple times within a day or two until 'camera-ready' outputs are produced.
triggers: need for a deliverable/artifact with an imminent deadline or session
clear, bounded technical objective (figure update, pipeline conversion, notebook run)
momentary focus blocks (deep-dive chat sessions / assistant-driven tasks)

phases.description: Rapid creation of code/artifact (same day)
Iterative fixes and hardening (hours-to-day)
Export / produce final artifacts (CSV, PNG, PDF, runnable script)

patterns.name: Research ↔ Product dual-track (simultaneous paper/experiments and commercialization prep)
patterns.description: The user runs research and experimental work (papers, model ablations, evaluation artifacts) in parallel with productization activities (MVP definition, landing pages, pilot partners, fundraising), shifting emphasis between the two as needed.
triggers: research progress that yields publishable/usable artifacts
product opportunity recognition or fundraising timeline
external deadlines like conference submissions or investor outreach

phases.description: Research & experimentation (models, figures, ablations, manuscript framing)
Artifact generation (figures, datasets, reproducible notebooks)
Productization & GTM prep (landing pages, demo scripts, pilot recruitment, pitch materials)
Fundraising / outreach / pilot execution

patterns.name: Decision-to-action lock-in behavior
patterns.description: When confronted with higher-stakes choices (accelerator picks, flagship project selection), the user seeks explicit commitment mechanisms, rubrics, and lock-in periods before fully committing—indicating a meta-pattern of defeating indecision by formal process.
triggers: high-stakes opportunity requiring prioritization (accelerator apps, fundraising)
multiple competing ideas or uncertainty about what to scale
desire to limit future switching costs and force progress

phases.description: Open consideration and idea accumulation
Seek rubric / decision framework and commit-level (time-based) constraint
Formal commitment or locked-in experimentation period

patterns.name: Accelerator / Application-Driven Sprint
patterns.description: A focused, short-lived burst of work producing investor/accelerator-ready artifacts (one-pagers, pitch copy, application text, demo assets, video scripts). Activities prioritize polish, packaging, and evidence claims rather than deep R&D.
triggers: Accelerator/application deadlines (SkyDeck)
Planned investor outreach or fundraising ask
Need to package product for external reviewers

phases.description: Trigger / deadline identification (accelerator/app deadline or investor outreach opportunity identified)
Rapid content consolidation and rewriting (one-liners, asks, fund allocation, GTM language)
Asset production sprint (demo assets, video script, images, production workflow)
Submission / prep for interview (application pasted, tactics updated, acceptance probability estimated)

patterns.name: Exploration → Positioning Pivot
patterns.description: Start with a capability-driven exploration (hardware or clinical framing) then quickly reorient to a different go-to-market or positioning (e.g., from medical/hardware-first to data/software-first or to non-medical pilots).
triggers: Legal/name risk or competitive intelligence (trademark searches)
Practical pilot constraints or timeline mismatch with target (e.g., SkyDeck deadline)
New evidence or reframing that reveals better non-medical use-cases

phases.description: Capability-grounded exploration (identify technical strengths, initial target domain)
Evidence collection / early pilot data gathering
Reassessment of market/legal fit (trademark/IP signals, pilot feasibility, time-to-market)
Pivot / narrowed or altered positioning (new SAM, different GTM focus)

patterns.name: Tool Procurement → Immediate Integration Sprint
patterns.description: Acquire a physical/tooling asset and then run a concentrated technical integration and validation effort to make it operational in days rather than weeks/months.
triggers: Need for ground-truth data for validation
Concrete pilot or experiment start
Gap in capabilities that can be solved by off-the-shelf hardware

phases.description: Identify candidate ground-truth or integration tool during product/validation planning
Procure/acquire the tool quickly
Rapid hands-on integration (SDK work, streaming setup, usage notes)
Operationalize for pilot/validation (data export, live streaming, collection)

patterns.name: Legal/IP Risk → Formal Decision Path
patterns.description: When IP or trademark risk is discovered, the workflow shifts to a formal decision process that documents estimates, constraints, and next steps (inventorship analysis, cost estimates, counsel engagement).
triggers: Trademark or prior registration discovery
Desire to formalize IP (patent) or protect technology
Institutional co-inventorship concerns (university affiliation)

phases.description: Flagging risk (USPTO search, institutional IP policy noted)
Information-gathering (statute references, counsel inputs, inventorship checks)
Budget and route estimation (cost to patent, PCT vs US-only, next procedural steps)
Decision to proceed, narrow claims, or rebrand

archetypes.name: Productization & Programs
archetypes.description: Projects that move from an asset or idea to an explicit product/service: broad exploration narrows to an MVP or packaged offering, followed by coordinated GTM, recruitment, and iterative scaling. These are often revenue- or growth-oriented and persist across months with many checkpoints.
defining_features: Long lifespan (months) with many state changes/decisions
Explicit monetization / revenue/growth metrics or GTM artifacts
Moves from exploration → concrete offer (syllabus, pricing, outreach drafts, pilot materials)
Parallel workstreams (marketing, recruiting, legal/branding occasionally)
Repeated reframing and iterative launches rather than one-off prototypes

archetypes.name: Research & Technical Prototyping
archetypes.description: Work that is research-first: idea → focused literature/architectural framing → short prototyping or manuscript/experiment preparation. Most items here are academically framed, evaluation-driven, and tend to have low churn in the conversation (few rapid edits) but can include longer-running research projects.
defining_features: Few transitions per item (concept/experiment focused) with many single-session interactions
Clear research deliverables (papers, related-works, evaluation plans)
Movement from architecture/idea to targeted experiments or writing
Often constrained to venue/acceptance choices or evaluation metrics
Occasionally spawns longer-running engineering threads but mostly stays research-scoped

archetypes.name: Tooling & Infrastructure Prototypes
archetypes.description: Libraries, pipelines, and architectural prototypes: the user either evaluates tools or builds lightweight infra prototypes. These projects show short, intense engineering iterations geared toward a working component that can be integrated into other projects.
defining_features: Short to mid lifespan (days–weeks), often prototype-focused
Frequent architecture/implementation decisions (concurrency, memmap, batching, caching)
Tight coupling to other projects as reusable components
Behavioural pattern: shortlist/evaluate → pick-a-default → deep implementation for demo
Often surfaces operational tradeoffs (cost, concurrency, environment) after initial build

archetypes.name: Short Rapid Sprints & Fixes
archetypes.description: One-day or similarly short interactions: small feature implementations, design requests, debugging bursts, and quick planning tasks. These usually produce immediate, concrete outputs and then become quiet.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Single-day intense debugging burst / Rapid Prototyping Burst
defining_features: Very short lifespan (same-day or negligible span_days)
Small number of transitions (creation + a couple edits/diagnoses)
Output-oriented: a fix, a design iteration, or a concrete how-to/workflow
Often diagnostic or implementation-specific (failing run, implementation detail, style prompt)
Low long-term follow-up; either handed off or archived after the burst

archetypes.name: Productization & Org-building
archetypes.description: Long-running, cross-cutting initiatives focused on go-to-market, organizational setup, and monetization. These projects accumulate many iterations over weeks–months, spawn complementary threads (branding, grants, legal), and prioritize packaging, outreach and revenue mechanics.
defining_features: High transition volume and long time-spans (repeated reframing and messaging edits)
Focus on GTM / monetization (pricing, outreach, grants, pilot planning)
Cascading spawn of related projects (brand, legal, funding)
Periodic major sprints followed by lower-cadence maintenance

archetypes.name: Research & Hardware Experiments
archetypes.description: Technical, experiment-driven projects (ML models, sensing hardware, domain research) that move between literature/feasibility work and pragmatic prototypes. Often includes hands-on debugging, dataset prep, and parallel aims of paper-writing and prototype demos.
defining_features: Start with literature/architecture questions then move to small-scale prototyping or experiments
Frequent single-day or short debugging bursts (hardware/firmware tweaks)
Dual goals: publishable insights (papers) and reproducible prototypes/demos
Tooling and data-collection are common blockers (datasets, instrumentation)

archetypes.name: Tooling / Retrieval & Integration POCs
archetypes.description: Architecture-first, tooling-focused work: compare or design retrieval/processing pipelines (RAG, vector DBs, library choices) and spin up short proofs-of-concept to validate integrations and flows. Behavior is exploration → focused POC → standardization.
defining_features: Architecture and stack discussions followed quickly by a small POC or demo
Short series of focused transitions (idea → POC → code/snippet generation)
Concentration on integration choices (LangChain/LlamaIndex, vector DBs, scraping/AST parsing)
Often ends in a pragmatic selection or a reusable pattern across projects

archetypes.name: Short Deliverables & Creative Sprints
archetypes.description: Concise, deadline-friendly creative work that aims for polished outputs (video scripts, one-pagers, visualizations, packaging). These are rapid ideation-to-delivery efforts with low long-term maintenance.
defining_features: Tightly-scoped outputs (scripts, visuals, descriptions) produced quickly
Low number of follow-ups after delivery (polish then archive or handoff)
Often triggered by a specific external need or pitch/application
Creative/branding tasks intermingle with technical deliverables (visuals, packaging)

archetypes.name: Early-stage Ideation & Small-blocked Experiments
archetypes.description: Short-lived idea captures and early scoping projects that remain at ideation or small-MVP stage. They often have minimal transitions and frequently stall on environment or decision friction (dependency problems, human-in-loop constraints) before deeper commitment.
defining_features: Low transition counts — captured ideas or feature lists without sustained build activity
Frequent blockers: environment/dependency stalls or human-in-loop feasibility concerns
Behavior is: generate concept → sketch features → pause until decision or resource allocation
Good candidates to either fast-PoC or archive; often surface again in productization arcs

archetypes.name: Research → Product Exploration
archetypes.description: Projects that start as technical or market exploration, quickly crystallize into concrete architectures/MVP plans, and are treated as potential product opportunities. Behaviorally these items show multiple early transitions (architecture, tradeoffs, pivots) and explicit move toward prototyping, demo scripts, or sales/validation activity rather than immediate shipping.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Explore → Narrow → Build → Ship or Stall
defining_features: Multiple architecture/positioning pivots early
Explicit MVP/POC planning and demo scripts
Moves from research/ideation into sales/pilot or technical PoC
Sometimes long-tailed (one item shows multi-week activity) but many remain short-lived proof phases

archetypes.name: Tool Evaluation & Integration
archetypes.description: Projects that are primarily focused on surveying, benchmarking, and comparing tooling or libraries, then choosing and integrating a preferred option. Work shows structured shortlists, focused evaluations/POCs, and decision-oriented transitions rather than marketing or hiring work.
defining_features: Clear shortlist / comparison mindset (3+ candidates considered)
Fast, focused tests or small POCs
Decision-orientation: choose or recommend a stack for reuse
Short calendar life in dataset (front-loaded evaluation activity)

archetypes.name: Academy / Program Productization & Hiring
archetypes.description: Curriculum, cohort programs and the operational threads that make them real: syllabus creation, marketing copy, prerequisite courses, and hiring of instructors/staff. Behaviorally these items produce many coordination artifacts (brochures, prerequisites, role definitions) and spawn hiring/ops entities in quick succession.
defining_features: Low per-item transition count (planning/ops focus rather than technical bursts)
Rapid creation of marketing & operational artifacts
Immediate coupling of productization work with defined hiring needs
Very short observed spans (administrative/configuration oriented)

archetypes.name: Rapid Prototyping & Monetization Sprints
archetypes.description: Small-scope product pushes that favor the fastest validation path: scope down, build a tight MVP or asset, and measure early traction or monetize (merch drop, daily product, small shipped app). These show quick pivots and early traction or explicit monetization framing.
defining_features: Fast scope pivots toward the minimal experiment that can show traction
Early metrics or explicit monetization plans recorded
Short, intense activity leading to an immediate deliverable (MVP, drop, landing)
Often followed by either scaling or deprioritization once traction is measured

archetypes.name: Individual Short Bursts — Debug / Training / Personal Prep
archetypes.description: One-off, high-focus personal projects: competitive programming problems, debugging sessions, training plans, or historical résumé items. They follow concentrated bursts of edits/decisions and often either finish quickly or are archived as personal progress artifacts.
defining_features: High-intensity, short-lived iteration cycles (debugging, training plan creation)
Concrete, bounded deliverables (working code, training schedule, competition prep)
Often personal/skill-oriented rather than product/commercial
Lower long-term activity after the initial burst (archival or occasional follow-ups)

archetypes.name: Strategic long‑horizon platforms
archetypes.description: High‑importance, cross‑cutting projects that the user treats as persistent pillars. These accumulate architecture notes, resume bullets, prioritized scopes and often spawn many dependent threads; activity is front‑loaded but continues as a low‑cadence, long‑running theme.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Long-running Iterative Development with Periodic Re-evaluation
defining_features: Multi-week to multi-month lifespan with periodic updates
High strategic priority (top‑3 or resume‑level references)
Early heavy architecture / planning followed by sporadic maintenance
Spawns related subprojects and references (org, infra, pitch, repo)

archetypes.name: Research → pragmatic prototype experiments
archetypes.description: Technical, researchy projects that start with architecture and tradeoff conversations then quickly narrow to pragmatic MVP or evaluation plans. Typically focused on tooling, models, or algorithmic prototypes and intended to produce a testable PoC or spec.
defining_features: Architecture/sketch → shortlist of concrete technical choices
Short runway to a hands‑on prototype or developer handoff
Tooling and model evaluation emphasis (repos, weights, infra)
Often recorded with concrete MVP approach (greedy/genetic, Mapbox, Streamlit, etc.)

archetypes.name: Asset → Monetization / productization pushes
archetypes.description: Projects explicitly oriented toward turning curricula, content, tools or capabilities into revenue: pricing hypotheses, outreach stacks, marketing assets and early sales/pilot plans are produced rapidly and prioritized for launch.
defining_features: Explicit go‑to‑market / pricing / outreach activity in early events
Creation of marketing collateral, outreach prompts, pricing drafts or sales spreadsheets
Short, time‑boxed pushes aimed at pilots/customers/enrollment
Often follows recognition of an asset (curriculum, content, capability) that can be packaged

archetypes.name: Personal experiments & short operational sprints
archetypes.description: Personal learning, wellness, or one‑off operational tasks: short, tightly scoped experiments or campaigns aimed at behavior change, learning, or a single deliverable. These are low‑friction, low‑scope and usually finish or stabilize quickly.
defining_features: Personal / wellness or study focus rather than productization
Low scope, few dependencies, usually launched and shaped in a single session
Defined baselines and targets (e.g., rest HR target) or short study plans
Rapid decision → short execution → either iterate or archive

archetypes.name: One-shot / Administrative & Quick Drafts
archetypes.description: Short, low-effort items created in a single session (or single conversation) that produce a finished artifact or a concrete answer. Behavioural signature: 1–2 quick transitions, same-day span, no continuing iteration.
defining_features: 2 transitions (create + one update) typical
Span ~0 days (same-day closure)
Produces an immediately usable deliverable or single definitive note
Low follow-up activity / low long-tail maintenance

archetypes.name: High-intensity short setup / sprint
archetypes.description: Multi-step, concentrated bursts of work across a short window to configure infra, resolve a tricky engineering problem, or push a prototype across the finish line. Behavioural signature: several rapid transitions within hours or a day, focused troubleshooting or setup, then handoff or quiet.
defining_features: High transition density (37 updates) compressed into <1 day
Tasks are operational (provisioning, config, model training fixes)
Outcome usually a saved artifact, provisioned system, or checkpoint
Often follows with rapid drop in activity or handoff/archival

archetypes.name: Research → Pragmatic prototype (ML / data / infra experiments)
archetypes.description: Technical research and experimentation that quickly converges to a pragmatic end-to-end prototype or developer-facing fix. Behavioural signature: engineering/research focused, short targeted updates (diagnosis, data fixes, training attempts), emphasis on reproducible artifacts (npy, checkpoints, scripts).
defining_features: Multiple small technical edits (data loaders, preprocessing, pipeline flags)
Produces reproducible artifacts (checkpoints, scripts, saved numpy arrays)
Bias toward hosted/OSS pragmatic choices and short Colab/train runs
Often bridges pure research and a minimal runnable demo

archetypes.name: Productization / Monetization push
archetypes.description: Projects that take an existing capability or idea and push it toward a commercial test or GTM asset. Behavioural signature: tooling selection, MVP artifacts (copy, pricing, funnels), outreach prep or automation infra, and explicit monetization framing.
defining_features: Explicit GTM / outreach or monetization artifacts (pricing, CSVs, landing copy)
Tooling selection and integration (Apollo/Clay, n8n, Google Workspace)
MVP-oriented: funnels, lead magnets, pre-warm steps
Mixture of product and ops work (infrastructure + pitch materials)

archetypes.name: Personal brand & website (iterative theme)
archetypes.description: Longer-running, cross-cutting personal-brand work: drafting voice/positioning and multiple iterations of site copy and content templates. Behavioural signature: heavier early iteration and occasional later reframing, mixes editorial decisions and tactical copy artifacts.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Long-running theme with heavy early activity and sporadic maintenance
defining_features: Multiple revisits and tone/positioning changes across weeks
Early concentrated edits (punch-up drafts, image prompts) then slower refinement
Mixes strategic framing (voice, achievements) with tactical deliverables (copy, CTA changes)
Often spawns related items (image prompts, testimonials, templates)

archetypes.name: Flagship / Long-term Platform Projects
archetypes.description: Projects that are treated as multi-year commitments or platform efforts: they receive repeated, substantive design/architecture work, spawn related sub-projects (repos, spinout plans), and are framed as the user's primary product bets. Behaviorally these items have higher-than-average update counts and longer observed lifespans (when activity is tracked) and show a pattern of heavy early investment followed by sustained, lower-cadence iteration.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Long-running Iterative Development with Periodic Re-evaluation
defining_features: Multiple rounds of scoping, architecture and roadmap work
Positioned as a product/organization-level commitment (spinout / ARR targets / multi-year plan)
Higher transition counts and measurable multi-week activity spans
Produces reusable assets referenced by other projects (repos, agent patterns, IP)

archetypes.name: Research & Technical Experiments
archetypes.description: Narrow, technical investigations that begin as research questions or evaluation experiments and move toward pragmatic prototypes or paper-writing. Behaviorally these projects are quickly scoped, focus on experiments/ablations/evaluation scripts, and show short, concentrated update patterns with emphasis on reproducible artifacts (figures, scripts, evaluation pipelines).
defining_features: Focus on experiments, metrics, and reproducible scripts/figures
Short, task-oriented update sequences (diagnosis → tweak → evaluate)
Often results in a paper, a focused prototype, or a decision to pivot
Frequent use of pragmatic hosted/OSS tools rather than large bespoke builds

archetypes.name: Short Intense Sprints / Timeboxed Activities
archetypes.description: Timeboxed, high-cadence efforts that occur over days: travel planning, trip execution, or rapid exploratory proofs-of-concept. These items show several rapid transitions within a small span and then drop to low activity (dormant or complete).
defining_features: High update density over hours–days (itineraries, short POCs, market scans)
Concrete immediate outputs (itinerary, proof-of-concept notes, short market lists)
Quick drop-off in cadence once the timebox ends
Often triggered by travel, calendar constraints, or near-term opportunities

archetypes.name: Idea Incubation & Early-stage Planning
archetypes.description: Fuzzy-to-concrete idea work: brainstorming, mind‑maps, draft outlines, MVP scoping, market research and early GTM thinking. Behaviorally these projects typically appear with 1–2 recorded transitions, short or zero tracked spans, and current state summaries that are 'idea / draft / planning' rather than built or shipped.
defining_features: Low recorded update counts; items are primarily drafts, outlines, or requirement lists
Fast moves from fuzzy idea to concrete checklists or MVP plans once prioritized
Includes personal projects, planning, and early market-research tasks
Frequently followed by a decision point: move to prototype (promote to other archetypes) or archive

archetypes.name: Core research ↔ product long-runs
archetypes.description: Projects that combine deep technical research, datasets and experiment work with productization, GTM and IP work. They show many updates over weeks/months, spawn supporting artifacts (pipelines, figures, datasets), and alternate between research iterations and commercialization tasks.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Research ↔ Product dual-track (simultaneous paper/experiments and commercialization prep)
defining_features: High total activity (many transitions) spread over weeks→months
Parallel research artifacts (papers, datasets, eval pipelines) and product work (landing pages, naming, legal)
Frequent context switches between experiments and GTM/IP tasks
Produces reusable artifacts referenced by other projects

archetypes.name: Tool evaluation → integrate
archetypes.description: Short-lived, focused projects that start as surveying or evaluating tooling/options and quickly converge to a recommended stack or integration plan. Typically low transition count per item (initial creation + decision) and often used as building blocks for other work.
defining_features: Small number of clear state changes (idea → shortlist/eval → decision/prototype)
Fast movement from exploration to explicit recommendations (tooling + stack suggestions)
Often environment- or integration-focused (sometimes blocked by deps)
Serves as inputs or dependencies for larger projects

archetypes.name: Rapid prototyping bursts
archetypes.description: Short, high-density engineering or design sprints producing a working prototype, demo-ready artifact, or PRD in a day(s). Multiple rapid edits and iterations happen, then activity falls off sharply.
defining_features: Many updates in a very short window (hours→days)
Goal-oriented: produce a runnable demo, PRD, or visual artifact quickly
Stabilizes quickly and enters a quiet/maintenance state
Low ceremony: focused technical iteration rather than long planning

archetypes.name: Asset → monetization push
archetypes.description: Projects that treat an existing or nascent asset (content, curriculum, pilot concept) and quickly pivot toward concrete monetization experiments — pricing, GTM materials, pilot structures and outreach drafts.
defining_features: Starts from an identified asset (content, deck, market map)
Rapid ideation of pricing and pilot/packaging options
Creation of GTM artifacts (content calendars, pricing, outreach copy)
Short decision horizon: either run pilots or fold into other products

archetypes.name: Personal goals & health experiments
archetypes.description: Personal, behavior-change or health-related projects where the user moves from acknowledgement/diagnosis to active planning and incremental attempts. These projects often include commitment mechanisms, medical or pharmacologic evaluation, or structured training plans.
defining_features: Personal stakes drive explicit plans (medication evaluation, rehab options, study schedule)
Mixture of research/education and scheduled commitments
Moderate cadence: a few updates as plans solidify or treatments are tried
Use of commitment mechanisms or structured programs to defeat indecision

archetypes.name: Rapid research → pragmatic prototype (Rapid Prototyping Burst)
archetypes.description: Short, focused technical or research experiments that move a concept to a small end-to-end test or prototype within a day or two. Behavioural signature is low transition count (often creation + one update), short lifespan, and concrete output requests (pipeline, prompts, demo plan, filtered data).
defining_features: Creation and one quick substantive update (2 transitions typical)
Span measured in hours or same-day edits (span_days ≈ 0)
Outputs: pipeline sketches, prototype plans, filtered datasets or immediate analysis results
Leans on pragmatic hosted/OSS tools and templates to get to a working artifact fast

archetypes.name: Deep iterative research / dual-track experiments
archetypes.description: Projects that require multiple rounds of iteration, data alignment, experiments and/or manuscript prep. Behavioural signature is several updates across days, explicit deliverables (aligned CSVs, test matrices, paper drafts/reviews), and parallel research/workflow artifacts.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Research  Product dual-track (simultaneous paper/experiments and commercialization prep)
defining_features: Multiple updates over several days (3+ transitions common)
Produces reproducible research artifacts (aligned CSVs, test matrices, reviewer-perspective notes)
Mix of experiment work and manuscript/paper-facing outputs
Often follows with downstream productization or submission (papers, conference/journal prep)

archetypes.name: Short deadline-driven personal & planning sprints
archetypes.description: Personal or short-scope projects that start fuzzy and are turned into concrete artifacts quickly (essays, travel plans, diets, learning routines). Behavioural signature: small-to-medium bursts of edits, high perceived urgency or deadline orientation, and clear deliverables (revised draft, itinerary, 7-day plan).
defining_features: Mix of personal-development, application, and planning work
Often driven by an external deadline or format requirement (applications, trips, diets)
Higher transition outliers (essay drafts) but many 1–2 update quick wins
Deliverables are polished text or concrete plans (itinerary, essay draft, meal plan)

archetypes.name: Productization / monetization & accelerator push
archetypes.description: Work that moves ideas toward product, GTM, or commercialization: curriculum design, pricing/outreach, accelerator prep, and purchase/procurement decisions. Behavioural signature is a short exploratory phase followed by concrete go-to-market materials, pitch assets, or demo preparation and explicit monetization framing.
defining_features: Focus on GTM artifacts: curriculum, landing pitch, pricing, outreach templates, accelerator materials
Often spawns parallel tasks (applications, pilot outreach, hardware procurement)
Mix of quick idea → product sprints and short follow-up refinement
Tendency to seek early pilots, paid experiments, or accelerator validation

archetypes.name: Cascading startup / product spawn
archetypes.description: A core company or product idea that rapidly fractures into many parallel operational tracks (pitching, market analysis, pilot planning, investor materials, hardware packaging). High coordination across complementary threads; work spawns many related entities in a short window and then follows both sprint and longer-tail maintenance patterns.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Cascading Project Spawn from a Core Idea
defining_features: Many related sub-projects created within days of core idea
Mix of technical, GTM, legal, and operational threads
High early coordination (pitch decks, outreach, pilot planning)
Some threads continue as longer-running maintenance or fundraising efforts

archetypes.name: Research → pragmatic prototype & eval
archetypes.description: Deep technical/research work that runs experiments, ablations and modeling while producing reproducible artifacts (notebooks, scripts, figures) and paper drafts. Behavior shows short, repeated experiment cycles and concurrent productization / paper-outlet thinking.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Research  Product dual-track (simultaneous paper/experiments and commercialization prep)
defining_features: Experiment-driven cadence: ablations, few-shot runs, plotting and reproducible artifacts
Short, repeated bursts of technical updates (notebooks, model analyses)
Parallel concern for paper framing (PerCom, PhD advancement) and practical prototyping
Artifact outputs: CSVs, PDFs, notebooks, and scripts that support both research and demos

archetypes.name: Short-form deliverable / deadline sprints
archetypes.description: Concise, narrowly-scoped projects created to produce a specific deliverable quickly (application materials, short scripts, articles, master prompts, program blueprints). Low lifespan, small number of transitions, outcome-focused.
defining_features: Very short lifespan (hours-to-days) and few updates
Deliverable-oriented (scripts, applications, articles, blueprints)
Polish and packaging prioritized over deep R&D
Often triggered by deadlines or opportunity windows

archetypes.name: Tool / personal optimization & procurement
archetypes.description: Evaluation and procurement of tooling or personal systems (hardware packaging, OBS recording workflow, supplement procurement) followed by immediate integration or consolidation. Low transition counts but concrete configuration/procurement outcomes.
defining_features: Tooling/procurement focus with concrete integration steps (CAD, carts, OBS configs)
Low iteration count once a preferred approach is chosen
Outputs are operational (shopping carts, CAD prototypes, hotkey scenes)
Often precedes or supports other projects (recording for pitch videos, supplements for performance)

archetypes.name: Pragmatic MVP Commit (fast decision + lean tooling)
archetypes.description: Projects that move from idea to a concrete, narrowly-scoped MVP in a single short burst of decisions. The user rapidly narrows options, chooses a pragmatic/no‑code or managed tooling path to avoid building bespoke infra, and defines a short time-boxed deliverable (weeks). Activity is minimal after the initial commit unless traction demands follow-up.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Exploration → Shortlist → Commit (and Pragmatic Simplification / Lean Pivot)
defining_features: Very few transitions (creation + one decisive update)
Same‑day or single-session decision to pick a tool/architecture (no-code/managed chosen)
Explicit, small MVP scope defined (2–4 week deliverable)
Behavioral signature: trade complexity for speed to get an early demo/pilot

archetypes.name: Seeded Project with External Stakeholder Tie‑in
archetypes.description: Projects that are instantiated and immediately linked to an external stakeholder, investor, or backer as part of early positioning. The primary early action is adding affiliation/validation (investor, backer) rather than lengthy internal iteration. These show quick, low-frequency updates focused on signal/packaging rather than product build.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Cascading Project Spawn from a Core Idea
defining_features: Minimal internal edits after creation; early update is association with external party (investor/backer)
Work emphasis on fundraising/positioning signals rather than immediate heavy engineering
Likely to spawn parallel tracks (pitch, legal, resume/personal positioning) even if not yet visible in activity counts
Behavioral signature: fast external validation/labeling as first tangible step

archetypes.name: Core ML & Retrieval Platform
archetypes.description: Tools, libraries and infra that are investigated, iterated on, and then integrated as the persistent backend for models, training, retrieval, and evaluation. These items tend to be revisited over months, become cross-project dependencies, and spawn small test harnesses and config artifacts.
defining_features: Multi-week to multi-month engagement with repeated revisits and updates
Moves from discovery/experiment to integrated, cross-project dependency
Includes both production-facing services (vector DBs, orchestrators) and research infra (model libs, data memmaps)
Often spawns small test harnesses/configs (fake clients, processor configs) to validate performance/scaling

archetypes.name: Frontend, Media & Demo Tooling
archetypes.description: UI, deployment and media tools chosen for demos, landing pages, and student-facing deliverables. Behavior: short-to-medium evaluation followed by pragmatic selection for shipping demos or course materials; occasional troubleshooting bursts for integration/embedding.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Multi-option Tool Triage 12 pick one 12 integrate (with occasional replacement)
defining_features: Short-to-medium evaluation windows tuned to 'what ships fastest' for demos
Often paired with media processing/embedding work (video/audio encoding, hosting)
Activity spikes around demo/demo-fix tasks and deployment choices
Tends to be chosen for UX polish / teaching examples rather than core research

archetypes.name: Rapid Scrape & Automation POCs
archetypes.description: Small, focused tool sets used for short-lived information-gathering POCs and one-off automation tasks (scraping docs, extracting APIs, quick checks). Usage pattern is quick spin-up, run/fix, then quiet.
defining_features: Low transition count with very short spans — fast experiments to fetch or validate information
Used to answer specific questions (docs scraping, plagiarism checks) rather than become long-term dependencies
Often combined in short scripts/one-offs and then archived

archetypes.name: Hardware & Edge Integration
archetypes.description: Physical devices and minimal intermediary hardware used to capture data or validate streaming/edge workflows. Behavior: quick procurement/bring-up and immediate integration into a prototype or collection pipeline.
defining_features: Very short-lived high-focus integration work (bring device online, stream data)
Fast hands-on debugging and configuration (firmware, Bluetooth/serial flows)
Often resolved to a stable streaming/data flow quickly and then becomes low-touch

archetypes.name: Core integration & execution stack
archetypes.description: Long-lived, repeatedly-referenced tools and platforms that the user returns to across architecture conversations and builds around. These items show sustained engagement (many transitions over months) and are treated as core execution or hosting pieces—candidates that move from evaluation into active integration and cross-project reuse.
defining_features: High transition counts and long span-days (months) — recurring mentions and updates
Referenced as part of cross-project architecture or as a platform-level dependency
Moves beyond discovery into concrete integration, testing, and reuse
Often serves as 'the stack' for experiments, demos, or production prototypes

archetypes.name: Shortlist & experimental backends
archetypes.description: Tools, models, or small libraries that appear as evaluated candidates: short-lived appearances, low update frequency, and treated as options to be tested or shortlisted. Behaviourally these are discovered, noted, and sometimes used in quick PoCs but rarely show long-term, high-cadence integration in the dataset.
defining_features: Low transition counts and short lifespans — early-stage evaluation mentions
Often part of a shortlist or comparison set rather than the permanent stack
Includes both model backends and small tooling candidates
Used for targeted experiments, demo prep, or as potential replacements

archetypes.name: Ops & security checklist (required components)
archetypes.description: Operational and security primitives that are surfaced as required pieces of an architecture (orchestration, session store, credential vaults, proxies, OCR/CAPTCHA, model stacks, protocols). These items typically appear as checklist entries or recommended components rather than the objects of deep, repeated experimentation.
defining_features: Appear as 'must-have' components in architecture conversations (low churn, prescriptive)
Low transition count per item but collectively form the ops backbone
Often surfaced together as a grouped recommendation / checklist
When one is chosen, integration is pragmatic and focused on reliability and security

archetypes.name: Quick-prototype & single-day fixes
archetypes.description: Small, tactical tooling or snippets used during short, intense sessions: debugging bursts, one-off integrations, visualization/formatting choices, or immediate environment fixes. These show very short spans and only a few transitions — behaviorally they are quick spikes that are closed out fast.
defining_features: Very short lifespan (hours to a day) and low transition counts
Tactical: used for immediate problems (parsing, diagramming, env fixes, tab consolidation)
Often accompanied by a single concrete deliverable (diagram, fix, exported tabs)
Behaviorally bursty and then quiet — minimal long-term follow-up

archetypes.name: Single-day diagnostic snapshots
archetypes.description: Tools/processes that appear briefly as part of a focused system snapshot or troubleshooting session. They get observed, annotated as suspects/causes, and then either dismissed or recommended for a quick action the same day.
defining_features: Very short span (same-day appearances)
Low number of updates after initial observation
Behavioral signature: diagnostic + rapid recommendation (quit/close/monitor)
Tied to an immediate problem snapshot (performance, CPU/RAM)

archetypes.name: Blocked-by-environment friction
archetypes.description: Tools the user attempts to adopt or run but which are stalled by configuration, dependency, or access problems. Activity is punctuated by diagnostics, remediation steps, and repeated follow-ups until environment issues are resolved (or remain blocked).
defining_features: Multiple follow-ups over days-to-months while resolving environment issues
Concrete blockers: missing PATH, incompatible package imports, DNS/Manage UI confusion
Lifecycle dominated by troubleshooting and guidance rather than feature evaluation
Often paired with assistant-supplied remediation steps

archetypes.name: Outbound / GTM tool evaluation & adoption
archetypes.description: Sales, outreach, enrichment and operational tooling that go through multi-option triage and short evaluations before the user picks and integrates one (sometimes retains alternates). These tools are discussed both as price/examples and for concrete integration into outreach workflows.
defining_features: Shortlist of candidates, price/details compared and used in GTM artifacts
Moderate number of revisits across weeks/months as integration and config happen
Outcome-oriented: selection leads to configuration (email DNS, workspace provisioning, enrichment setup)
Mix of SaaS and workflow/no-code automation tools

archetypes.name: Model & compute research → procurement
archetypes.description: High-technical research and procurement items (models, agent frameworks, hardware/infrastructure) that are explored, compared, and sometimes valued or procured. Activity spans research, tradeoff comparisons, and occasional asset valuation or integration planning.
defining_features: Technical comparisons of models/frameworks and infrastructure
Mix of research citations (papers/repos) and tangible assets (servers, clusters)
Often leads to a procurement or a pragmatic hosted/OSS choice for prototyping
Longer tails for orchestration/integration conversations and occasional valuation events

archetypes.name: Academy productization & voice/no-code stack
archetypes.description: Items tied to the user's educational product (Lucid Academy): persona tooling, voice/TTS providers, and lightweight/no-code platform decisions intended to produce an MVP or a customer-facing workflow quickly.
defining_features: Deliberate shift toward lean/no-code choices for rapid MVP delivery
Persona and voice-agent design paired with concrete integration targets
Short bursts of definition followed by operationalization efforts (voice integration, form follow-ups)
Behavioral signature: productization-focused evaluation rather than deep R&D

archetypes.name: Personal health & monitoring tools
archetypes.description: Personal health/wellness tools recommended or tracked for ongoing monitoring. These are low-churn, recurring monitoring or supplement stacks the user considers adopting into daily routines.
defining_features: Recommended for daily or ongoing tracking rather than one-off evaluation
Low-frequency updates in the log (adoption/recommendation events)
Actionable: intended to change daily behavior or supplement intake
Behavioral signature: health-monitoring rather than product/technical integration

archetypes.name: Core orchestration & runtime stack
archetypes.description: Tools and components that the user adopts as a persistent backbone for automation/ML workflows. These items show multiple integrations, configuration work (JSON/CLI fixes), and become the reused infrastructure across projects.
defining_features: Multiple transitions over weeks→months (adoption & config iterations)
Acts as orchestration/orchestral layer shared across prototypes
Requires configuration/operational attention (JSON/CLI fixes)
Becomes a cross-project dependency rather than a one-off experiment

archetypes.name: Shortlist / candidate tools under evaluation
archetypes.description: A set of external services and libraries the user surveys and sometimes trials briefly. These tend to show low activity counts (initial discovery + a small number of checks) and are frequently mentioned as fallbacks or enrichment options.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Multi-option Tool Triage → Pick One and Go All-in
defining_features: Low transition counts (discovery + brief test/mention)
Short-lived, exploratory interactions (sometimes long-tail mentions)
Framed as candidate/fallback for a specific pipeline step (enrichment, scraping, vector DB)
Often evaluated in parallel with other options rather than deeply integrated

archetypes.name: Rapid prototyping / short sprint artifacts
archetypes.description: Small, focused engineering bursts that produce working prototypes, demo workflows, or one-off utilities. They show concentrated activity in a short window and then quiet down or are handed off.
defining_features: High-density work in hours–days to produce a runnable artifact or demo
Multiple rapid state changes then a sharp drop in activity
Often tied to a concrete deliverable (workflow JSON, local Docker run, parsing code)
Prone to environment/dependency friction (local Docker failures, unhealthy containers)

archetypes.name: Research & model experimentation
archetypes.description: Technical exploration of models, quantization and deployment tradeoffs. These entities are investigated with deeper technical analysis, recipes, and decisions about pragmatic deployment for constrained hardware.
defining_features: Technical tradeoff analysis (FP32/FP16/PTQ, LoRA recipes)
Mix of long-running investigation (models) and short experiments (APIs)
Leads to pragmatic deployment choices (quantization targets, lightweight models)
Produces reproducible commands/recipes and integration notes

archetypes.name: Business & personal operations infra
archetypes.description: Non-core but operationally important tools and services used to run the user's workspace, web presence, payments and personal productivity/commitment tools. They tend to have low activity but can persist as ongoing operational concerns.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Long-running theme with heavy early activity and sporadic maintenance
defining_features: Operational state or configuration focus (site migration, device pairing, installability)
Lower transition frequency but longer-lived mentions (ops/maintenance)
Tie into business or personal workflows (payments, workspace, commitment tools)
Often surface as bottlenecks or admin tasks rather than R&D work

archetypes.name: Personal health experiments
archetypes.description: Bio / wellness items the user experiments with to affect sleep, recovery or cognition. These are treated as experiments with dosing/expectations and occasionally benchmarked against wearables.
defining_features: Low-frequency mentions tied to a trial or regimen decision
Often discussed with mechanistic rationale and dosing
Benchmarked against wearable metrics or subjective outcomes
Treated as iterative experiments rather than one-off tool adoptions

archetypes.name: Hardware procurement → immediate integration
archetypes.description: Physical devices and local peripherals that are acquired/identified and quickly plugged into workflows. Behavioral signature: low number of conversational transitions, very short active windows (hours–days), hands-on troubleshooting or simple verification steps, followed by either operational use or archival notes.
defining_features: Physical/hardware focus (sensors, audio, cameras, wearables, adapters)
Short, hands-on integration and verification steps
Low conversational/update count per item (quick check-ins)
High signal of procurement + immediate technical setup or troubleshooting

archetypes.name: Research & rapid experimentation (notebooks, models, datasets)
archetypes.description: Artifacts used for model development, evaluation, and experiment tracking. Behavioral signature: iterative technical edits, medium-to-high transition counts for some items, mixture of short spikes (notebooks, analyzers, spreadsheets) and longer-running experiment containers (model sets, datasets) as the user tunes experiments and collects reproducible outputs.
defining_features: Code/notebook/dataset-first items (analysis classes, notebooks, model sets, experiment trackers)
Frequent iterative edits or structured experiment rounds
Mixture of short prototype spikes and a few longer-running experiment artifacts
Outcomes oriented toward reproducible outputs (plots, PNGs, saved spreadsheets, stable notebooks)

archetypes.name: Tool evaluation & adoption (including environment friction)
archetypes.description: Software/tooling options that the user is evaluating for integration into workflows. Behavioral signature: discovery and short trials, environment/configuration or path issues sometimes encountered, followed by a decision to trial further or defer integration.
defining_features: Explicit evaluation/testing phase (attempted installs, activation instructions, CLI upgrades)
Often blocked briefly by environment/dependency friction (PATH, install conflicts)
Short conversational footprint while orthogonally important for future integration
Outcome tends to be either integration planning or deferred adoption

archetypes.name: Exploratory on-chain / crypto experiments
archetypes.description: Short-lived, high-focus experiments in the crypto / on-chain tooling and markets space. Behavioral signature: quick live transactions, conceptual tooling discussions, and rapid assessment of trading / dispute-resolution options — typically low transition counts and short windows but high informational value.
defining_features: Finance/chain-focused experiments (bridging, markets, oracle concepts)
Rapid forward movement (transactions or single-session investigations)
Often informational: concept understanding or opportunistic alpha hunting
Short-lived but occasionally references longer windows (e.g., Polymarket noted across weeks)

archetypes.name: Go-to-market & content/productization assets
archetypes.description: Tools and artifacts explicitly chosen or created to package, present, or monetize work (landing-page tools, virality/system prompts). Behavioral signature: decisive selection or construction with the aim of external-facing product/marketing output; low technical iteration in the conversational trace.
defining_features: Marketing / GTM orientation (landing page design, virality prompts)
Deliberate selection or crafted artifact for outreach or investor-facing materials
Low conversation frequency once created; intended for reuse in pitches or content
Tightly goal-directed (design/formatting/voice) rather than technical prototyping

archetypes.name: Rapid model prototyping / short debugging bursts
archetypes.description: Short-lived, high-focus experiments around models and training artifacts: quick creation, immediate fixes or tweaks, and rapid stabilization or rename. Activity concentrated in hours–days with few state changes.
defining_features: Low absolute number of transitions (2–3) clustered in a very short time window
Fast fixes/edits (debugging NaNs, adding preprocessing, naming/label changes)
Outcomes: working prototype, small stable artifact, or a rename/cleanup rather than long-term maintenance

archetypes.name: Tool procurement → immediate integration sprint
archetypes.description: Physical tool/device acquisition followed by an intense hands‑on integration and validation push: SDK usage, streaming setup, usage notes and operationalization soon after procurement.
defining_features: Higher-than-average transition count concentrated over a short-to-medium window
Concrete procurement and active engineering integration (SDK, live telemetry, streaming)
Outcome oriented toward operationalization for pilot/validation (data export, live streaming)

archetypes.name: Candidate tool evaluation / shortlist
archetypes.description: Discovery and lightweight evaluation entries: the user catalogs options, records capabilities/constraints, and flags items as candidates for future integration. Activity is low-touch (documentation, capability notes) and often short-lived until a decision or deeper evaluation occurs.
defining_features: Minimal transition counts (often 2) representing 'first-seen' + a notes/update event
Entries are research/notes rather than deep integration (capability summaries, limitations, connector examples)
Serve as candidates for later shortlist/selection rather than immediate shipping artifacts

archetypes.name: Persistent research & canonical concepts
archetypes.description: Long-running thematic threads and core technical concepts that the user deepens, references across projects, and revisits sporadically. These items often start as conceptual study or architecture-level discussion, receive technical deepening (examples, tradeoffs, canonical notes), and then persist as reusable knowledge or project foundations.
archetypes.typical_lifecycle: Long-running theme with heavy early activity and sporadic maintenance
defining_features: Low-to-moderate transition rate per item (2–5) with high variance due to a few long-span items
Large spread in lifespan driven by a handful of long-lived anchors (e.g., Transformers, RAG)
Tendency to produce canonical explanations, reusable workflows, or curriculum-level material
Cross-project references and reuse (concept deepening → cross-project reuse)
